name: Shoegaze
description: Guitars drenched in distortion and reverb, buried vocals, and walls of sound — named for the way guitarists stared at their effects pedals on stage instead of the crowd.

name: Neo-Psychedelia
description: Modern artists reviving 60s psych-rock textures — swirling production, hazy melodies, and studio experimentation — filtered through contemporary pop and rock songwriting.

seeds.album: Man It Feels Like Space Again

name: Dream Pop
description: Lush, atmospheric pop built around washy guitars, reverb-soaked vocals, and a hazy, melodic softness — adjacent to shoegaze but generally gentler and more song-focused.

seeds.album: So Tonight That I Might See

name: Post-Punk
description: The angular, artier fallout from punk — jagged guitars, prominent basslines, and a colder, more experimental edge, laying groundwork for goth, indie, and new wave.

name: Synthwave
description: Retro-futuristic electronic music built on analog-style synths and drum machines, drawing heavily on 1980s film scores and video game soundtracks.

name: Vaporwave
description: A deliberately slowed-down, chopped-up collage of 80s/90s corporate music and elevator jazz, wrapped in a nostalgic, digital-decay aesthetic.

name: City Pop
description: Glossy, funk- and jazz-inflected Japanese pop from the late 70s and 80s, built for cruising — smooth grooves, lush production, and an optimistic, breezy feel.

name: Trip Hop
description: Downtempo, sample-heavy electronic music that grew out of Bristol, UK — moody, bass-driven, and cinematic, blending hip hop breaks with dub and jazz textures.

name: Math Rock
description: Rock built on odd time signatures, intricate interlocking guitar parts, and unconventional song structure — technical and angular, but still driven by feel.

name: Post-Rock
description: Rock instrumentation used to build slow-building, largely instrumental compositions — often quiet-to-loud dynamics, long runtimes, and a focus on atmosphere over verse-chorus structure.

seeds.album: Lift Your Skinny Fists Like Antennas to Heaven
The Earth Is Not a Cold Dead Place
Millions Now Living Will Never Die

name: Hyperpop
description: Maximalist, internet-native pop — pitched-up vocals, distorted synths, and glitchy production pushed past conventional pop polish into something more chaotic and playful.

name: Noise Rock
description: Rock pushed toward abrasive extremes — dissonant guitars, feedback, and a confrontational, often deliberately unpolished production style that favors texture and intensity over melody.

name: J-Rock
description: Japanese rock music spanning visual-kei theatrics, noisy post-hardcore, and arena-scale pop-rock — a broad, distinctly Japanese scene with its own aesthetic and star system.

name: Bossa Nova
description: A cool, understated fusion of samba rhythm and jazz harmony that emerged in late-1950s Brazil — soft vocals, nylon-string guitar, and unhurried, conversational melodies.

name: Tropicália
description: A late-1960s Brazilian movement that fused samba, rock, psychedelia, and avant-garde ideas into something defiantly eclectic — as much a cultural and political statement as a musical style.

name: IDM
description: Electronic music built for headphones rather than the dancefloor — intricate rhythm programming, unconventional sound design, and a more composerly, experimental approach than typical dance genres.

seeds.album: Music Has the Right to Children

name: Baggy
description: Late-1980s/early-90s Manchester scene blending indie guitar rock with dance rhythms and acid house grooves — loose, shuffling beats under jangly, hooky songwriting (a.k.a. Madchester).

name: Noise Pop
description: Pop songwriting run through distortion and feedback — hooks and melody still up front, but wrapped in fuzzed-out guitars and a rougher, more DIY production style.

name: Shibuya-kei
description: A stylish, genre-blending Japanese pop movement from Tokyo's Shibuya district in the 1990s — mixing lounge, bossa nova, French pop, and electronic influences into something cosmopolitan and playful.

name: Indietronica
description: Indie rock songwriting built with electronic production and instrumentation — synths, drum machines, and studio manipulation applied to guitar-band sensibilities.

seeds.album: The Bones of What You Believe

name: Psychedelic Rock
description: 1960s rock aimed at recreating or evoking altered states of consciousness — extended jams, studio effects, unconventional song structure, and an exploratory, mind-expanding sensibility.

seeds.album: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
The Piper at the Gates of Dawn
The Psychedelic Sounds of the 13th Floor Elevators

name: Jazz Fusion
description: Jazz improvisation combined with the electric instrumentation, rhythms, and volume of rock and funk — virtuosic playing over grooves borrowed from outside the jazz tradition.
